production.note: US model years. Consumer Guide (Tom Appel) covers the '1991-95 Toyota MR2': redesigned for 1991 and 'entered its final season without change' in 1995. KBB lists a 1995 MR2 'Turbo Coupe 2D' (kbb-1995-mr2).

body.note: Sports Car Market: buyers could choose 'a fixed-roof coupe (rare in the U.S.) or one with a sunroof or T-tops'. T-tops are a roof option, not a separate body.

displacementL.note: Consumer Guide: 'a 2.0-liter unit that made 200 horsepower, borrowed from the Toyota Celica All-Trac Turbo'; KBB: '4-Cyl, Turbo, 2.0 Liter'. Consumer Guide elsewhere says '2.1-liter', an evident slip. No opened page gave the cc figure.

drivetrain.note: Mid-engine, rear-wheel drive; inferred from the description.

transmission.note: 'A 5-speed manual transmission was standard, with 4-speed automatic optional for nonturbo models.'

powerHp.note: PROVISIONAL (one article plus a database). Quote (Consumer Guide, Tom Appel): "Turbo coupes got a turbocharged engine: a 2.0-liter unit that made 200 horsepower, borrowed from the Toyota Celica All-Trac Turbo." KBB 1993 Turbo Coupe: "Horsepower: 200 @ 6600 RPM" (kbb-1993-mr2-turbo); KBB 1992: "200 @ 6000 RPM" (kbb-1992-mr2-turbo); Sports Car Market: the Turbo 'hit the magic 200 mark' (scm-mr2).

weightLb.note: PROVISIONAL (databases). 1991 Turbo coupe, 5-speed manual. Quote (iSeeCars, 'Turbo 2dr Coupe'): "Curb Weight | 2758 | lbs". KBB's 1992 Turbo Coupe 2D agrees: "Curb Weight: 2758 lbs." (kbb-1992-mr2-turbo; next model year). For 1993 both databases give 2,822 lb (kbb-1993-mr2-turbo; iSeeCars 1993), so the weight rose with the 1993 model year.

sources.title: That's Mister Two to You (Jeff Zurschmeide, 17 June 2024)

provisionalNote: Power (200 hp) rests on one article (Consumer Guide) and KBB (database); weight (2,758 lb) rests on iSeeCars (1991) and KBB (1992), both databases. A Toyota press kit or brochure, or a major magazine spec panel, for the 1991 MR2 Turbo would replace them.
